text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday's Albanian neuwspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- An editorial blames the government for resorting to violence against demonstrators protesting across the country at the collapse of pyramid schemes and urges it to tell the truth.
- The newspaper reports one dead in Fieri district, 110 km from Tirana, following clashes of some 10,000 people and police on Sunday in the central square.
- State-run television completely served Berisha's regime by broadcasting fake scenes with red ink instead of people with bloodied faces.
- The newspaper says foreign correspondents were allegedly put under pressure by officials who did not want them to report accurately about Sunday's protest in Tirana.
- People in the northern town of Shkodra warn they will stage protests unless the government gives up the 25.5 billion leks ($250 million) it seized in savings deposited in pyramid schemes.
- The newspaper quotes National Bank governor Kristaq Luniku as saying that depositors will get back their money only after the courts rule on the fate of the pyramid schemes.
- The appeal court freed Pali Miska, a former communist minister, arrested for alleged involvement in crimes against humanity.
- Parliament passed a bill exempting some students from military service.
- The Socialist Party is determined to head popular protests across the country, its secretary-general Rexhep Mejdani told a news conference.
- Berisha's regime is worried by the possibility of unrest.
